subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should OpenClaw make ordinary exec nonzero subprocess exits a normal completed tool result by default, or require an explicit accepted-exit-code/allow-nonzero policy?
rationale: The code path is narrow, but the behavior is a product/API contract because some existing automations may depend on nonzero exec exits producing tool-error or cron-error state.

options.title: Default completed nonzero exits
options.body: Treat normal exec exits 0-125 as completed results with exitCode and output, keeping spawn, timeout, signal, denial, and shell 126/127 failures on the error path.

options.title: Opt-in accepted exit codes
options.body: Preserve current default error classification but add a documented exec option such as acceptedExitCodes or allowNonzeroExit for semantic scripts.

options.title: Document workaround only
options.body: Keep the current behavior and document the wrapper pattern, accepting that semantic exit-code scripts need extra user logic.

recommendation.title: Default completed nonzero exits
recommendation.body: Treat normal exec exits 0-125 as completed results with exitCode and output, keeping spawn, timeout, signal, denial, and shell 126/127 failures on the error path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows ownership around the exec/tool runtime boundary, and the decision spans runtime behavior, cron delivery, and compatibility policy.
